// for: a condition loop drains a queue through a bool method, and
// three-clause loops count up, down, and to a bound a call computed.
// continue still runs the post clause and break skips it; the loop
// variable is one flat slot that outlives the loop; the per-iteration
// ctx.Err() check is the only bound a condition loop keeps.
q := queue("a", "b", "c");
buf := bytes.NewBufferString("");
for q.More() {
	buf.WriteString(q.Next());
}
assert.Equal(tb, "abc", buf.String());

c := counter();
for i := 0; i < 4; i++ {
	c.Add(i);
}
assert.Equal(tb, 6, c.Sum());
assert.Equal(tb, 4, i);

d := counter();
for j := 3; j > 0; j-- {
	d.Add(j);
}
assert.Equal(tb, 6, d.Sum());

n := strlen("gozero");
e := counter();
for k := 0; k != n; k++ {
	e.Add(1);
	continue;
	e.Add(100);
}
assert.Equal(tb, 6, e.Sum());

f := counter();
for m := 5; m <= 9; m++ {
	f.Add(m);
	break;
}
assert.Equal(tb, 5, f.Sum());
assert.Equal(tb, 5, m);
